request.question: What are the best external managers buying now, and do we own or trade any of it?

run_result.question: What are the best external managers buying now, and do we own or trade any of it?

answer.stance: Mostly against them, though not firmly.
answer.text:
Our largest active trades sell what the better external managers bought, chiefly Kioxia and Weichai Power. Each of those ideas rests on two buyers at most [EF1] [US2].

Kioxia is the clearest clash. We net sold USD 83 million across seven accounts, while two others bought [US2]. The better half of managers bought it in each of the last three month-ends, and it sits in their tested top-50 basket [EF1]. Renesas (USD 86.2 million sold), Resonac (USD 42.5 million) and Murata (USD 25.5 million) follow the same pattern [US2]. We also sold USD 31 million of Weichai Power A shares [US2]. JD Health is the one confirm: our EMA Active strategy bought USD 36.6 million, and the stock was up 6.8% a month later [US4]. Across the book, 56 strong conflicts worth USD 4,024 million slightly outweigh 45 strong confirms worth USD 3,722 million [US2].

On Kioxia, outside research leans against our selling. Every broker rates it a buy [B6] [B7] [B4]. Brokers put it at two to three times earnings for the year to March 2028, against three to five times for peers [B6] [B7] [B11]. Capacity for 2027 is sold out [B1], and management said on 13 November that data-centre demand exceeds supply through 2027 [EC1]. A former Kioxia insider said it meets only about half of data-centre demand, but warned that selling only flash memory leaves it exposed to rivals who can cross-subsidise [X1].

Weichai stays open. GIC's analyst cut it from 60 to 30 basis points overweight in September 2026, citing a US order banning Chinese equipment from data centres [R1] [R6]. The managers' case is a 14% rise in third-quarter recurring profit [B12], genset shipments climbing from 500 to 1,300 units [B13] and a valuation of about 9 times 2027 earnings with a 5% yield [B20]. Since then, four brokers have cut their targets [B27] [B26] [B21] [B28], and October heavy-truck sales fell 13% [B22].

The quant score backs only some buys. Laurus ranks top fifth [EQ2], and our small sell has lost as the stock rose 5.7% [US3]. Bilibili and Z.AI rank bottom fifth [EQ7] [EQ6]; one of our accounts bought USD 12.9 million of Z.AI before it fell 46.9% [US10]. Quant scores cover MSCI emerging-markets stocks only, at 31 October [EQ1]. Timing gains are raw price moves, not risk-adjusted [US4].

Two things would change this view: a US ruling on Chinese power equipment, expected around late December [B29] [N1], and evidence that our Japan technology selling was rebalancing rather than a deliberate view.

points.claim: The best external managers' buy list is real but thin. The eight score-3 names, all in the tested top-50 basket, are Laurus Labs, Adani Energy Solutions, Haitian Intl, Weichai Power A, JD Health, Komatsu, CR Beer and Kioxia. No name has more than 2 distinct buyers. India and China lead, and Industrials and Staples are the main sectors.
points.text: The buy list is real but thin. Eight names score 3 at the Oct-26 month-end [EF1]. Two of the eight cannot be quant-checked: Haitian Intl was not found in the EM universe after three attempts [EQ1] [EQ8] [EQ9], and Komatsu is a Japan (developed-market) stock, outside the quant universe by design. Read this as a few managers' ideas, not broad consensus.

Komatsu had no trades [US8]. The real active conflicts are larger: Weichai and the Japan tech names [US2].

answer.text:
